applies_why: The judge text gives UNDERDETERMINED because the sign's sense is left open, which is the kind of openness K-S2 governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand': one reading treats an open verse-sense as a reason for UNDERDETERMINED; the other treats two simultaneous senses as both standing and not open.
why: The judge used an open sense of Isaiah 7:14 as its ground for UNDERDETERMINED, exactly what K-S2 forbids when a verse carries two senses.
